Title: BYD names geopolitics as biggest hurdle, puts US passenger car sales on hold
Article:
SINGAPORE: The number one challenge to expansion for BYD is geopolitics, Stella Li, BYD's ​executive vice president, said on Thursday, months after the Chinese company's chairman said it aims to become the world's largest automaker within five years.
"When we do business, we want to do something and have certainty and visibility then we can control and then we can invest. But with geopolitics, you never understand what's the angle and what they are doing," said Li at the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore.
Li said the company has decided to not sell passenger cars in the US for now despite being in the US for "a long time" as it is "complicated."
"We don't have clarity, visibility and stability there so we're saying let's hold and not to go to the US for passenger cars at this moment."
Li said BYD has no plans to partner with other Chinese companies given its leadership in various areas such as storage and solar panels. "We're a leader in multiple businesses, not only cars," she said.
Li also said it's been difficult to hire enough people in China and the company hopes to use industrial robots in future.
She said BYD's stock on the Hong Kong exchange was "super undervalued" compared to US companies, given that the company is an engineering firm and not just a car company.
She also said Nvidia remains a "very strong" chips partner for BYD.--REUTERS

Title: Vietnam busts ring accused of stealing 2,700 cats for slaughter
Article:
HANOI: Police in Vietnam have arrested 12 people accused of stealing 2,700 cats and selling them for slaughter in Ho Chi Minh City, the Ministry of Public Security said this week.
The suspects, aged between 16 and 39, were arrested on suspicion of stealing the cats with the intention of selling them for food.
The men were found with cat traps, cages and fur-removal equipment, according to a ministry statement
Police rescued dozens of cats during the raid
Cat meat dishes are still served in some parts of Vietnam, particularly in rural areas, where they are sometimes marketed as "mini tiger" and believed by some consumers to have medicinal properties
The arrests followed complaints from residents about the nighttime disappearance of their pet cats, the statement said.
Authorities identified Luu Thanh Binh, 39, as the alleged ringleader and distributor. Investigators said he also bought live cats and resold them to customers seeking cat meat
To supply the operation, Binh allegedly worked with several accomplices who recruited younger people to capture cats in residential neighbourhoods. Police said he also supplied traps used in the thefts
The group operated mainly between 11pm and 4am, using fish bait and traps placed outside homes with pet cats. Captured animals were quickly collected and transported for sale, police said
Police have returned 13 of the cats to their owners and said the remaining animals were being cared for by animal welfare group HavePaws while authorities continued efforts to identify their owners. - REUTERS

Title: Who holds the gavel? COP31's unusual Australia-Türkiye deal
Article:
AUSTRALIA and Turkiye are co-hosting the 31th United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) next month but the highly-unusual decision to share leadership has raised questions about how the climate summit will unfold —and who holds the power.
Both countries had fought to host the high-profile event, forcing a compromise under which Turkiye would stage COP31 but Australia would run the formal negotiations.
The two delegations insist they are working closely together and have pledged steady and predictable leadership at the summit starting Nov 9 in the Turkish city of Antalya.
But the dual-presidency model "has no precedent" at United Nations climate summits and its success is not guaranteed, said Anna Perez Catala from the Paris-based policy think tank IDDRI.
It "aims to showcase countries can work together even in difficult times, but could bring disagreements", she said.
The climate summits rotate between regional blocs, with the host normally selected by consensus after consultation among members of the relevant group.
Australia and Turkiye arrived at last year's COP in Brazil as rival bidders for the 2026 summit and a diplomatic stalemate ensued when neither would withdraw from the race.
Australia's bid enjoyed wider support but Turkiye did not relent, arguing it could bridge industrialised and developing nations and highlighting ample, affordable hotel capacity in Antalya.
After extensive closed-door talks, a compromise was reached: Turkiye would be COP31 president, host the summit and world leaders in Antalya, and design the "action agenda" that runs alongside the formal talks.
Australia's Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen was named "president of negotiations" and granted "exclusive authority" of the negotiations.
Additionally, pre-COP meetings are being held in Fiji and Tuvalu this week in a nod to Australia's original desire for the summit to have a Pacific focus.
The compromise resolved the hosting deadlock — but questions over the specifics soon emerged.
In April, when asked if he would have a role in the negotiations, incoming COP31 president Murat Kurum said Turkiye would "play a role anywhere, everywhere, because Turkiye is the COP31 president".
"At the end of the day, the decisions will be taken by the COP31 presidency," said Kurum, who is also Turkiye's environment minister.
In June, Bowen acknowledged there was some nervousness over the unique arrangement but said concerns were misplaced.
"I do understand because it's a new thing. But what we're doing actually has a lot of benefits and potential," he said in Bonn, Germany, during the mid-year UN climate sessions.
When asked who would bring down the final gavel at COP31, Bowen replied: "Kurum and I... Together."
Yet last month, when asked again to clarify this situation, Kurum stressed: "Turkiye is not co-chairing COP31 with Australia."
"In conducting those negotiations, Australia will work in consultation with the COP31 presidency, and ultimately the final decision rests with the COP31 presidency," he said.
Kurum and Bowen insist the arrangement is working smoothly, calling each other good friends and joshing about football when their national sides competed in this year's World Cup.
"We are genuinely working in harmony with Australia and our friends there... We have not experienced any problem so far, and we do not expect to encounter any in the future," said Kurum last month.
But it remains to be seen whether the novel arrangement works out.
"Historically, when there has been a lack of clarity of process or roles of presidencies at the COPs, it has diverted attention from the work at hand," said Germany's former climate envoy Jennifer Morgan.
The summit comes at a fragile moment for climate diplomacy: energy security concerns are high on the political agenda, trust in multilateral institutions is under pressure, and nations remain divided over tougher action on planet-heating fossil fuels.
A French government official said there was a "clear division of roles" between the two countries: "It's a new approach, so we'll see how it works in practice."
The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nearly 300,000 Nepalis at flood risk: Study
Article:
NEW DELHI: More than 1,400 people were killed and 5,000 remain missing after catastrophic floods hit Nepal in August – and a new study Thursday warned nearly 300,000 people face similar risks.
A tsunami-like wall of water and debris triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on the Nepal-China border on Aug 26 cut a swathe of destruction across the nation.
The disaster raised fears that similar floods could strike elsewhere as glaciers retreat and development expands across fragile mountain terrain.
The study, published in Scientific Reports, examined areas up to 50 kilometres downstream of 1,361 Himalayan lakes in Nepal and neighbouring parts of China and India.
"Our results demonstrate rapidly increasing exposure in Himalayan catchments," key study scientist C. Scott Watson, from Britain's University of Leeds, told AFP.
Scientists say climate change played a key role in the August floods.
Nepal, a country of around 30 million people that contributes only a fraction of global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost US$4.78 billion.
Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations last month that the flooding "was a warning to the world" about the rising dangers of climate change.
The study estimated 293,000 people live less than 50 metres above usual water flows, putting them potentially within reach of floodwaters.
And the area covered by buildings in potential flood zones increased by nearly 46 per cent between 2016 and 2023, the study found.
In the Himalayas, where rivers drop rapidly in height, giving them staggering power, even small changes in temperature or rainfall can have "disproportionate impacts" downstream, it added.
"Hazards are increasing as glaciers retreat, glacial lakes form and mountain permafrost thaws," Watson said.
"It was only last year that a smaller-scale glacial lake outburst flood, with associated fatalities and infrastructure damage, struck the same river channel as the recent August 26 disaster," the scientist added.
"The next step is to develop detailed hazard maps that we hope can inform land-use planning, infrastructure development and early warning systems."

Title: War shakes Netanyahu's support in Israel's north
Article:
On Israel's border with Lebanon where Hizbollah fired thousands of rockets and drones, previous backers of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu say they are rethinking how they will vote in the first election since the war. "Many I know were right-wing and were Bibi supporters, and today they're not," said plant nursery owner Sigal Malachi, using a nickname for Israel's longest-serving premier.
In traditional strongholds of Netanyahu support, many said they could no longer back his right-wing government in the Oct 27 vote, accusing it of failing to secure a lasting quiet with the resistance fighters.
Hizbollah, an Iran-backed Lebanese resistance group, began firing into Israel in October 2023 in support of Hamas following the deadliest-ever attack on the country.
The barrages altered life in northern communities, displacing tens of thousands of Israelis and forcing people like Malachi to close shop for several years. Northern Israelis are accustomed to incoming fire from the Lebanese side of the border, but they say that round of conflict was more intense.
"We grew up with Katyushas (rockets) and bombs," said Malachi, whose plant nursery reopened in March. "This war was different."
She described that "if you went outside, within a second you'd be running" for shelter.
The war was halted with a fragile ceasefire in November 2024, but evacuees were not allowed home until early 2025.
Life began slowly returning to normal, until the northern front reopened after the outbreak of the Iran war.
Maxim Zarbaylov, who was born in the former Soviet Union but has long lived in Nahariya, the northernmost Israeli town on the Mediterranean, is among those wavering.
"All my life I voted for (Likud), for Bibi Netanyahu... But this year I want to vote for (Gadi) Eisenkot," he said, referring to the former military chief who is Netanyahu's main election rival.
Hizbollah has repeatedly dragged Lebanon into conflicts with Israel, most recently in March with rocket fire at Israel in support of Iran.
Israel has in turn seized what it calls a "security zone" in Lebanon, where authorities say Israeli attacks have killed over 4,300 people.
The prolonged violence has left border residents in limbo.
"After Oct 7 we don't sleep well any more," said Malachi. "I've thought about leaving. But the roots are so deep that I'm staying."
In Shlomi, an Israeli border town, the enemy is a tangible presence behind a hill.
Shadi Tuma, who owns a supermarket there, prides himself on running the only one that remained open.
"This area is under a trauma we haven't seen before. There's anger. The government is unable to provide a comprehensive response.
"It's a huge psychological catastrophe. Not everyone is able to cope with a war that lasts three years."
The war has cracked the local support base for Netanyahu, Tuma added.
In the last elections in 2022, the premier's Likud party won 43 per cent of the vote in Shlomi, compared with 23 per cent nationwide.
Residents who backed Netanyahu "now want change because they no longer trust this government", said Tuma.
He said the high cost of living was a major complaint.
"Many people I see are struggling to make it to the end of the month."
For Tuma, the conflict is also personal.
He was born in Lebanon, the son of a fighter with the South Lebanon Army, a militia that fought alongside Israel in the 1980s and that had many fighters granted Israeli citizenship.
The war could have shifted longstanding political loyalties in towns like Nahariya, a sleepy resort of about 70,000 people.
In 2022, 38 per cent of voters there chose Likud. But Zarbaylov says there is anger over the failure to stop Hamas' unprecedented assault on the country.
"What happened on Oct 7, Bibi could have prevented it, but he didn't," he said.
Others believe only the current hawkish coalition can protect them.
Patrice Haddad retired to Nahariya from Paris a year ago, drawn by the town's "charm".
Israel's "Law of Return" allows any Jew anywhere in the world to immigrate and automatically receive citizenship.
Adjusting to life under the rockets was not simple at first.
"We were told we had 30 seconds to find shelter" after sirens blared, he said. "In reality, sometimes we only had 15, sometimes less."
The writer is from AFP

Title: Indonesia arrests three ferry executives over deadly Java Sea sinking
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian police have arrested three executives of the company that owned a passenger ferry that sank in the Java Sea last month, killing dozens of people, a spokesman said Thursday.
The Virgo Transport 8 was carrying 213 passengers and 30 crew when it lost contact after departing from Surabaya, Indonesia's second-largest city, on Java island, bound for Borneo.
The Indonesian suspects, who worked for the shipping company that owned and operated the ferry, stand accused of negligence, national police spokesperson Trunoyudo Wisnu Andiko said in a statement.
"The designation of suspect status is based on the results of the investigation... which identified indications of negligence, complicity, as well as aiding and abetting in connection with the ship accident," he said.
Police arrested the ferry's captain last month.
Dozens remain officially missing in the search operation that has retrieved 108 survivors to date. More than 80 people have been confirmed dead.
Marine accidents regularly occur in Indonesia, a vast Southeast Asian archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are often the cause.--AFP

Title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Seremban and Segamat highest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions remained concerning tonight, with 36 areas nationwide recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10pm.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Seremban in Negri Sembilan and Segamat in Johor recorded the highest API reading at 188.
They were followed by Nilai, Negri Sembilan (184); Bukit Rambai, Melaka (178); Kluang, Johor (178); Bandaraya Melaka (177); Tangkak, Johor (177); and Johan Setia, Selangor (177).
The Klang Valley was also affected, with Putrajaya recording an API reading of 174, followed by Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur (173), Shah Alam (172), Banting (171), Cheras (170) and Petaling Jaya (168).
In the east coast and northern regions, several areas including Rompin, Pahang (174); Bandar Indera Mahkota, Kuantan (166); Pegoh, Ipoh (160); Tanjung Malim, Perak (160); Kemaman, Terengganu (156); and Seberang Perai, Penang (128) also recorded unhealthy readings.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a Facebook post, said the haze was expected to persist in several parts of the country.
In the Klang Valley and surrounding areas, including Kuala Lumpur, Petaling, Sepang and Putrajaya, hazy conditions are forecast in the morning and at night, while thunderstorms are expected in some areas in the afternoon.
In Johor, districts including Segamat, Kota Tinggi and Muar are forecast to remain hazy throughout the day, in the morning, afternoon and at night, with no rain expected.
The lack of rain is expected to hamper efforts to improve air quality in the near term.
"Therefore, people in affected areas are advised to reduce outdoor physical activities, wear a suitable face mask if they need to go outside and drink sufficient water to prevent health problems related to the deteriorating air quality," it said.

Title: 'Stunned' Madrid mourns pensioner who sparked housing protests
Article:
MADRID: One of hundreds of housing protesters camping in central Madrid, Aitana Lopez felt duty-bound to pay tribute to a pensioner whose eviction sparked a movement that culminated in early elections.
The death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal on Wednesday drove a "stunned" Lopez to lay a candle on Thursday at an improvised shrine in the Spanish capital's Puerta del Sol square, the epicentre of the protests.
"Thank you for everything, we will never forget you," read a message on the candle, which accompanied flowers and a placard calling Abascal "the grandmother of an entire country."
Abascal, who used a wheelchair, died in hospital two weeks after her eviction from the Madrid apartment where she had lived for 70 years.
Taken away on a stretcher after the real estate company that owned the flat drastically hiked the rent, she became the face of Spain's long-running housing crisis and the catalyst for nationwide protests.
"She's the one who started all of this," Lopez told AFP, referring to the camps and demonstrations that have placed housing at the heart of a snap general election on Nov 29.
"At the very least, I wanted to come down, lay a candle... to make an appearance," said the 25-year-old, who studies fashion.
A small group of people huddled around the tribute in Sol on Thursday, some visibly moved, while tourists tried to navigate an obstacle course of tents and candles.
On Wednesday night, protesters in the square wept and embraced each other after learning the news. Hundreds marched towards parliament, some calling the death a "murder."
[[nid:1550850]]
A deal had been reached with the real estate firm allowing Abascal to return home at a lower rent, but she ultimately spent her final days in hospital.
"She didn't have to die this way. Maricarmen wanted to die in her house," said Valeria Racu, a spokeswoman for the Madrid Tenants' Union, which supported Abascal in her years-long legal battle against the company.
Luis Rodriguez, 64, said it was "outrageous" that an elderly woman was kicked out of her home, calling her "yet another victim" of Spain's ruthless housing market.
"She represented the last straw" of popular anger at unaffordable housing, said Rodriguez, who has lived in Madrid all his life, describing real estate prices in Spain as "crazy."
Attempting to respond to the popular pressure, the left-wing government hastily agreed two decrees that included greater protections against evictions for vulnerable tenants and the automatic renewal of contracts.
But the minority coalition failed to pass the measures in parliament, prompting Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call the early vote on Monday.
For Juana Sotillos, a 68-year-old pensioner, Abascal "has been used as a political tool by one side and the other", saying Sanchez "has done nothing" on housing during his eight years in power.
Another march is scheduled for Thursday evening from Sol to Maricarmen's former home in the upmarket Retiro neighbourhood, where candles and flowers have also been left by mourners.
Tenants' unions have called for a national minute's silence at noon (1000 GMT) on Friday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Stop treating government loans like grants
Article:
The government is making viability assessments mandatory before any new federal loans are approved. This is a welcome prudential move aimed at correcting a longstanding weakness in public lending.
The 2026 Auditor-General's Report had uncovered that only RM465 million, or five per cent, of RM9.27 billion in outstanding recoverable loans was collected in 2025.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong revealed in Parliament that RM578.32 million in repayment arrears for 23 loans were written off during the year.
This is precisely the sort of grim lesson the auditor-general's findings ought to elicit: stop treating loan approvals as the end of the process and the repayment as someone else's problems later.
We are talking public money being disbursed as federal loans here. The government has a duty and responsibility to ensure that money loaned out today does not become tomorrow's multi-billion-ringgit repayment headache.
Viability assessments for fresh loans need to be conducted before any approval is given and they ought to be done by independent parties and not by the very agency seeking any loan.
Rigorous stress tests should be standard operating procedure to ascertain what happens if revenue projections fall short, costs rise, interest rates change or projects in question are delayed.
Borrowers ought to be given clearly defined repayment milestones with early interventions built in when repayments are missed. Any loan restructuring should trigger a fresh viability assessment instead of earning an automatic repayment extension.
Since public money is involved, there must also be greater transparency about federal loans: how much is outstanding, which borrowers are in arrears, the frequency of loan restructuring and recovery action taken.
Ministries or agencies extending loans must clearly distinguish between commercial projects and projects serving a public or social obligation.
The latter ought not be dressed up and passed up as qualifying for loans simply to get around any lack of budgetary appetite for extending grants. Strict and very narrow criteria must be applied for loans for commercial projects by government and government-linked entities.
Any assessment for such projects ought to provide satisfactory answers as to why a government loan is required and why commercial loans may or may not be obtained instead.
Indeed, gone should be the day when the government extends loans for commercially unproven and non-viable projects.
The extent of delayed or non-recoverable payments of government-approved loans raises a host of related issues, foremost of which is the resources and manpower needed by the government in the loan-recovery process — up to and including legal action, as the deputy minister noted — before some, maybe most, of such loans are ultimately written off.
Far better, perhaps, for the government to extend either full or partial grants for worthy projects and gradually phase out the business of government extending loans for projects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorcyclist, pedestrian injured in viral Lebuh Chulia crash
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A motorcyclist was injured and a pedestrian suffered a fractured leg after a crash on Lebuh Chulia on Oct 5.
Northeast deputy police chief Superintendent Lee Swee Sake said police detected a 46-second video of the incident circulating on WhatsApp today.
He said investigations found that the crash occurred about 9.10pm when the 22-year-old motorcyclist was travelling from his workplace on Lebuh Chulia towards Jalan Patani.
"Upon reaching the scene, the motorcyclist collided with a 32-year-old pedestrian who was crossing the road," he said in a statement.
Lee said the motorcyclist sustained minor injuries, while the pedestrian suffered serious injuries, including a fractured leg, and was still receiving treatment in hospital.
"Initial investigations found that the accident was believed to have been caused by the motorcyclist's negligence in handling his vehicle, resulting in the collision with the pedestrian," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for careless and inconsiderate driving, which carries a jail term of up to a year and a fine of between RM4,000 and RM10,000 upon conviction.

Title: ICC says Philippine ex-president Duterte fit to be tried
Article:
THE HAGUE: Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte is fit to stand trial on charges of committing crimes against humanity during a crackdown on the drug trade, the International Criminal Court said Thursday.
"The chamber was satisfied that the accused is able to effectively exercise his fair trial rights in the proceedings," the court said of the 81-year-old, whose trial is due to start on Nov 30.
The judges' based their decision on the findings of an independent panel of experts and submissions from other interested parties and participants, said the ruling.
Duterte had the capacity to "understand the charges, understand the purpose and consequences of the proceedings, follow the course of the proceedings," said the experts, quoted in the court ruling.
He could also "understand the evidence, and instruct counsel in the preparation and conduct of his defence", they said.
The former leader appeared in person at the court for the first time in mid-September, faces charges over his "war on drugs" that killed thousands.
Duterte, who ruled the Philippines between 2016 and 2022 and before that was mayor of the southern city of Davao, is the first Asian former head of state to face trial at the ICC.
The tribunal prosecutes individuals for the world's worst crimes such as war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Duterte faces three counts of crimes against humanity, with prosecutors alleging his involvement in at least 76 murders during his offensive from between 2013 and 2018, during his time as mayor and president.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Schools in four states, KL, Putrajaya and Rompin to close
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Schools in four states, including one district in Pahang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya will be closed tomorrow following the worsening haze situation.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the closures involve all schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as schools in Rompin, Pahang.
She said schools in Perlis, Perak, Penang, Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan would operate as usual.
"I have directed all state Education Departments and district education offices to continue monitoring the haze situation and take immediate action if conditions required.
"I understand that any decision to close schools affects the daily arrangements of parents.
"Moving forward, we will ensure any decision to close schools is communicated earlier so parents have sufficient time to make preparations," she said in a Facebook post.
Fadhlina urged parents to continue following official updates from their respective schools, district education offices and state Education Departments.
"The safety and health of our children and school communities will always remain our priority," she said.

Title: Attack risks rise for tankers as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes
Article:
LONDON: Tankers are facing a higher risk of attacks and intimidation as they try to get critical shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran issued new warnings it would block routes that it has not authorised, sources said.
Last week already saw the biggest number of attacks on tankers in the key waterway since the Iran war began - cutting the number of vessels trying to get through to the lowest in more than two months.
Iran has now warned regional countries that any attempt to open new routes for oil exports would be considered hostile, a senior regional official close to Teheran told Reuters.
It was part of a plan agreed by both Iran's political leaders and its Revolutionary Guards, the official added.
"Iran has absolutely no intention of allowing control of the Strait of Hormuz to slip from its hands, and has plans ready to block routes that some regional countries have for exporting oil," a senior diplomat in the region briefed by Teheran told Reuters separately.
"This could involve missile and drone attacks on ships, or sending boats to scare ships away," the diplomat added.
"It plans to continue this policy of fear and threats," he said.
In recent months, Gulf oil producers have rushed shipments of oil through channels that hug the Omani side of the strait before transferring the oil in open waters in the Gulf of Oman with aerial support from the US, sources have told Reuters.
In the latest incident in the past 24 hours, projectiles struck a tanker some 51 nautical miles off the coast of Qatar inside the Gulf, British navy agency UKMTO reported.
Maritime security sources said the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged chemical tanker Acers had been hit by multiple projectiles north of Qatar's Madinat ash Shamal with minor injuries sustained by its crew.
"The Acers strike raises the prospect of a wider combat area affecting approaches to Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq," maritime risk intelligence group Pole Star Global's subsidiary Clearwater Dynamics said in a report on Thursday.
The vessel's operator, listed in shipping databases as Antigua and Barbuda-based Valvoria Shipping, could not be reached for comment.
"The recent spate of Iranian attacks seems to have dampened the appetite of shipowners to sail through the Strait," said Jakob Larsen, chief ​safety & security officer at shipping association BIMCO.
"The Iranian threat appears to have increased."
US President Donald Trump is weighing next steps against Iran, including whether to escalate strikes before or after the November midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress, as he presses a naval blockade meant to pile economic pressure on Teheran to reach a deal to end the conflict.
The war — and its US$3 billion monthly price tag — has become a key issue on the campaign trail.
Governments and energy companies have drawn oil from stockpiles to alleviate pressure in a global oil market facing unprecedented supply disruptions this year, also caused by the war in Ukraine.
The amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market is running low, ‌industry executives said at a forum in London this week, making the market more fragile and putting upward pressure on prices.
The impact of the crisis was increasingly rippling across the global economy.
Danish shipping group Maersk said on Thursday it was increasing its emergency fuel surcharge on inland transportation in the UK and Ireland due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
"There is no going back to the old world, no harboring back to the stability and the prosperity of the last several decades," Major General Paul Maynard, Assistant Chief of the Naval Staff with Britain's Royal Navy, told a UK Chamber of Shipping Riviera conference in London this week.
"A war at sea does not remain at sea."

Title: Dozens protest in Tokyo after Marine accused of murder in Okinawa
Article:
TOKYO: Dozens of protesters lined up in front of Japan's Foreign Ministry on Thursday after a US Marine was accused of killing a woman in the southernmost prefecture of Okinawa, many holding signs decrying crimes by US service members.
The case is the latest in a string of incidents stretching back years that have fuelled unease over the large US troop presence on the island chain near Taiwan and China, with US officials warning it could undermine ties vital to security in East Asia.
Public reaction to Anna Yagi's killing, however, has been muted compared with the mass demonstrations that followed the rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen in 1995.
Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Yagi, 39, in a hotel in the Okinawan capital of Naha last weekend and taking her wallet and backpack. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
Leaders of Thursday's protest spoke over loudspeakers about abuses by US service members and called on the government to respond, with others in the crowd rattling noisemakers in assent.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has called the killing "extremely brutal and heinous", and Tokyo said it had strongly protested to the US and demanded measures to prevent a repeat of such incidents.
Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of US forces globally. Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until 1972.
That presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel.
The US on Wednesday began a 48-hour pause of military operations and a ban on alcohol while troops undergo training on standards and discipline.
Service members have also been given a month-long curfew for a "period of reflection."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar extends condolences over deaths of three siblings in Pontian crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed his condolences over the deaths of three siblings killed in a road crash in Pontian, Johor, today.
In a Facebook post, Anwar also expressed his deepest sympathies to the victims' family and prayed that they would be given strength and resilience in facing the tragedy.
"May the souls of the deceased be showered with blessings and be placed among the righteous. Al-Fatihah," he said.
The three siblings, aged between eight and 18, were killed around 7.20am after they collided with a lorry travelling in the opposite direction while they were heading from Jalan Parit Haji Omar towards Kayu Ara Pasong on a motorcycle.
Pontian police chief Superintendent Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain said the pillion riders, aged eight and 11, died at the scene, while the 18-year-old motorcycle rider succumbed to his injuries at Pontian Hospital.
The 69-year-old lorry driver sustained injuries to his hands and both knees.

Title: Ex-prince Andrew search warrants quashed after police accept legal error
Article:
LONDON: British police on Thursday said that search warrants it secured to search properties linked to King Charles' younger brother Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had been incorrectly granted and must be quashed.
King Charles' younger ​brother was arrested on ‌suspicion of misconduct in public office in February and searches carried out at properties in Sandringham, eastern England, and Windsor.
Andrew was suspected of leaking confidential government documents to the late convicted sex-offender Jeffrey Epstein when Andrew was a British trade representative, between 2001 and 2011.
Police have not charged him and Andrew, the second son of the late Queen Elizabeth, has denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein, also saying he regrets their friendship.
The arrest of Mountbatten-Windsor, and the anger over his relationship with Epstein, left the British royal family facing one of its worst crises in 90 years.
Mountbatten-Windsor applied for the search warrants to be quashed and Thames Valley Police said it accepted that they had not been properly granted.
"We accept the position that the initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore these must be legally quashed," a Thames Valley Police spokesperson said.
"Legal proceedings are currently ongoing to decide how material seized during the searches will be managed and whether we can lawfully retain it in support of our ongoing investigation."
It said its criminal investigation which began after the release of millions of documents by the US Department of Justice relating to Epstein was still ongoing.

Title: Trump voters are not pumped about voting in the midterms, poll finds
Article:
WASHINGTON: Voters who backed Democratic former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 are far more enthusiastic about casting ballots this November than those who supported President Donald Trump, a Reuters/Ipsos poll found, in a potential warning sign for Republicans heading into the midterm elections.
The six-day poll, completed Monday, also found that men were more enthusiastic about voting and more certain to cast ballots than women, and that male voters showed signs of shifting toward Democrats.
That could signal erosion in Republican support among a demographic that was a pillar of Trump's 2024 victory.
Some 48 per cent of 2024 Harris voters said they were "very enthusiastic" about voting in the Nov 3 midterm elections, when control of both chambers of Congress is at stake.
By comparison, just 30 per cent of Trump voters said the same in the poll.
The findings add to evidence of an enthusiasm gap favouring Democrats and suggest potential cracks in the coalition that propelled Trump in 2024, when he won the popular vote.
That coalition was fuelled by strong support from men and gains among Hispanic voters and other demographic groups that shifted to the right in the 2024 election.
The poll also adds to a string of encouraging signs for Democrats, who are widely favoured to win control of the House of Representatives and remain competitive in the fight for the Senate as Trump's approval ratings have slipped amid voter concerns about the cost of living and the war with Iran.
Republican strategist Charlie Gerow said the poll's findings raise the stakes for his party's turnout efforts, though he expects the enthusiasm gap to narrow as concerns about what he described as far-left Democrats gaining power motivate Republican voters.
"The enthusiasm has to be ginned up among Republicans because turnout is what's going to determine the outcome of these midterm elections," Gerow said.
While Trump voters overwhelmingly plan to vote Republican and Harris voters are similarly inclined to vote Democratic, the president's 2024 supporters are less decided, with 13 per cent saying they aren't sure who to vote for in congressional elections, compared to seven per cent of Harris supporters who say the same.
The poll, which was conducted nationwide and surveyed 4,506 adults online, showed that just 32 per cent of Americans approved of Trump's presidency, holding at a record low first marked in a September Reuters/Ipsos survey.
The survey has a two percentage point margin of error.
Since taking office in January 2025, support for Trump has fallen across every major demographic group, including double-digit drops among Hispanics, men, rural and suburban voters, people without college degrees and evangelical Christians.
One notable shift has come among men, a group Trump won in all three of his presidential campaigns, including by a 12-point margin in 2024, according to a Pew Research analysis.
When asked how they would vote in a congressional race if the elections were today, men in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll picked Democrats over Republicans, 43 to 39 per cent.
The four-point Democratic advantage was the widest of Trump's second term.
Men consistently favoured Republicans in 2025 but since August have mostly favoured Democrats.
The warning signs for Republicans reflect growing voter concerns about the high cost of living amid a surge in gasoline and diesel prices following the war with Iran.
Trump launched the Iran attacks in February, despite pledging during his campaign not to start new conflicts and to lower costs for consumers.
Cost of living is the top issue on Americans' minds as they decide how they will vote next month, the Reuters/Ipsos poll found. Voters cite democratic values as the second biggest issue, followed by immigration.
Republicans continue to hold an edge among older voters, a crucial bloc in midterm elections, when seniors have historically accounted for an outsized share of the electorate.
Voters 50 and older still favour the Republican Party over the Democratic Party, 44 to 42 per cent, though that was down from an 8-point Republican advantage in December.
Still, the enthusiasm gap looms large for Republicans.
Among all the voters in the poll who said they were enthusiastic, 62 per cent said they were pumped about expressing opposition to Trump, compared to 36 per cent who said they were eager to support the president.
Linda Rivera, a 46-year-old Trump voter in Pennsylvania, said that while she would probably vote Republican if she casts a ballot, she is frustrated with both parties and feels "neither enthusiastic or unenthusiastic" about voting next month.
Rivera, a respondent in the poll, said concerns about widespread voting fraud - which have been repeatedly fanned by Trump and his Republican allies without evidence - have added to her doubts about whether she will vote.
"I have lost faith in the voting process," she told Reuters. "I have lost faith in both parties. Not just one."

Title: Tanjong Karang crash: 'Norawalysa was a caring, dedicated' teacher'
Article:
TANJONG KARANG: A special education teacher who was killed along with her two children in a crash on Jalan Raja Muda Musa here today was described as a dedicated and committed educator.
Norawalysa Mat Talpi, 44, a teacher with the Integrated Special Education Programme (PPKI) at SK Bestari Jaya, was remembered by parents and colleagues as a caring teacher who was well-liked at the school.
Parent Saridon Ratiman, 58, said his youngest daughter, Nur Afeeya Nayla, eight, was among the last pupils to see Norawalysa before leaving school around noon today.
"Her way of handling pupils was unique, and she was an educator who was never tired of teaching.
"My daughter's last encounter with her was when she was leaving school around noon. She even waved to her before we headed home," he said when met at the forensic medicine unit of Tanjong Karang Hospital.
Saridon said he learnt about the crash at about 3pm.
He extended his condolences to Norawalysa's family, praying they would be given strength and fortitude to face the tragedy.
A large number of family members, relatives and friends were also seen at the hospital to pay their last respects.
Norawalysa and her two children, Auni Syazana, 12, and Ahmad Syah Fawwaz, eight, are expected to be buried at the Kampung Parit Serong Muslim Cemetery tonight.

three people were killed

Title: 'Tonto' claims trial to 55 charges of bribing traffic cops RM62,900
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 'tonto' (lookout) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court today to 55 charges of giving RM62,900 in bribes to three traffic police officers between January 2022 and February this year.
Ang Lie Giap, 33, entered the plea after all the charges were read out before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin.
According to the charges, Ang was alleged to have corruptly given money to three traffic police officers from the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters, Negri Sembilan Police Contingent Headquarters and the Kesas Expressway EMPV Patrol Office, as an inducement for them not to inspect lorries during roadblocks.
The bribes were allegedly given in several transactions at several bank branches in Klang and Setia Alam, involving amounts ranging from RM700 to RM2,000.
In a separate case, a logistics manager of a company, R Yuvarajakumar, 42, also pleaded not guilty at the same court to 16 charges of giving RM4,200 in bribes to a Road Transport Department (RTD) enforcement assistant between May 2023 and October 2024.
According to the charges, the father of two was alleged to have corruptly given money to an enforcement assistant at RTD Wangsa Maju through several transactions into several bank accounts belonging to a woman at a bank branch in Sungai Buloh, as an inducement for the officer not to inspect lorries.
All the offences were allegedly committed under Section 17(b) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for imprisonment for up to 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the bribe, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The prosecution in both cases was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Asmaa' Zamri.
Earlier, Asmaa' offered bail of RM15,000 for Ang and RM10,000 for Yuvarajakumar, with one surety each, together with additional conditions that the accused report to the MACC office once a month, surrender their passports and not interfere with prosecution witnesses.
However, lawyer K Theivaendran, representing Ang, applied for the bail to be reduced to RM10,000 and for his passport not to be surrendered to the court, as his client needed to travel abroad frequently for religious matters.
He also informed the court that the accused's wife was pregnant and expected to deliver their first child today.
"The accused is not a flight risk and works helping to manage his father's chicken farm business, earning between RM3,000 and RM3,500 a month," said the lawyer, who appeared together with lawyers Varghese Onny, Tee Yuan Sheng and Tee Kar Weng.
Lawyer Datuk Dr Aswandi Mohamed Hashim, representing Yuvarajakumar, meanwhile applied for the bail to be reduced to RM5,000, saying it was his client's first offence and that he needed to support his mother, who suffers from asthma.
The court allowed Ang and Yuvarajakumar to be released on bail of RM15,000 and RM5,000 respectively, with one surety each, and ordered them to report to the MACC office once a month and not interfere with witnesses.
Yuvarajakumar was also required to surrender his passport.
The court set Dec 3 for mention.

Title: Schools in Selangor, Melaka to close tomorrow over haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All schools and educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MoE) in Selangor and Melaka will be closed from tomorrow due to worsening haze.
In Selangor, state Education Department director Datin Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim said all educational institutions under the ministry would remain closed until further notice.
She said the decision was in line with the
MoE's media statement
issued today following unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
Schools were required to conduct home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) to ensure learning continuity during the closure.
"Teachers and support staff would work from home throughout the closure, subject to current instructions and operational needs," she said.
Parents and guardians were advised to follow official updates from the department, particularly on when schools and educational institutions would reopen.
"Parents and guardians are also advised not to make any assumptions about the reopening of schools and to refer only to official announcements from the department and MoE," she added.
Schools were also told to continue monitoring the situation and prioritise the safety, health and welfare of students and education personnel.
In Melaka, state Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman said all schools under MOE would be closed tomorrow after API readings in key areas of the state exceeded 150.
He said the closure would also cover all religious primary schools under the Melaka Islamic Religious Department, as well as kindergartens.
He did not rule out the possibility of schools remaining closed next Monday if API readings remained above 150 throughout Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

Title: Report lodged over sexual AI content involving Kedah students, teachers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has received a complaint over the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) to create and distribute sexual images and videos involving students and teachers at a school in Kedah.
In a statement, MCMC said the misuse of AI to create or distribute sexual content that could affect the safety, dignity and wellbeing of victims, particularly children, is subject to action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
It said licensed service providers also have child protection obligations under Section 18 of the Online Safety Act 2025 (Onsa).
"If convicted, a fine of up to RM500,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both, may be imposed.
"For offences committed against children, the penalty may include imprisonment for up to five years, subject to the provisions of the law," MCMC said.
It said the commission would cooperate with the relevant parties in the investigation.
MCMC reminded the public not to create, upload or redistribute sexual content involving or allegedly involving children, as such actions could harm victims and affect the investigation process.
Members of the public with relevant information are urged to channel it to the authorities through the appropriate channels.

Title: Three siblings killed in Pontian crash buried in single grave [WATCH]
Article:
PONTIAN: Three siblings killed in a motorcycle-lorry collision in Jalan Parit Haji Sirat here earlier today were buried in a single grave at the Kampung Parit Haji Siraj Muslim cemetery.
Nor Daniel Aiman Norlizan, 18, Nor Daniel Fikri, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha, 8, were buried at 7.30pm after funeral prayers at Masjid Jamek Kampung Parit Haji Siraj.
Their father, Norlizan Khamis, 42, thanked those who supported the family and helped with the funeral arrangements, including the schools, agencies and local residents.
The siblings were killed when the motorcycle they were on collided with a lorry about 7.20am.
Fikri and Naufa died at the scene, while Aiman died on the way to Pontian Hospital.
District police chief Superintendent Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain said the motorcycle had
collided with a lorry
travelling in the opposite direction.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving which carries a jail term of five to 10 years and a fine of RM20,000 to RM50,000 upon a first conviction.
Before the incident, their mother, Julaiha Munaji, 44, had told her two younger children that their
school was closed
because of the haze.

Title: PH unveils 'Melaka Rumah Kita' concept for state election
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan will introduce the 'Melaka Rumah Kita' concept in the upcoming Melaka polls, with its manifesto and vision for the state to be unveiled during the campaign.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the concept would outline the coalition's aspirations for Melaka, the livelihood of its people and the direction it intends to take the state if given the mandate.
He said 'Melaka Rumah Kita' would be built in stages, beginning with the opening of PH's main operations centre today, which he described as the "first pillar" of a larger structure to be introduced throughout the election period.
"What is Melaka Rumah Kita? Later, throughout the lead-up to the campaign and polling day, I will present our manifesto and vision regarding the future of Melaka, the lives of the people of Melaka, and what we envision for Melaka in the future," he said when officiating the centre.
Amirudin said PH would conduct a positive campaign by highlighting its offers and ideas for voters to evaluate, rather than relying solely on political rhetoric.
He said PH also had prior experience administering the state, including under the leadership of Adly Zahari, who served as Melaka chief minister in 2018.
"This is the foundation we are building. Melaka is our home and its cornerstone was laid long ago. Our friends in DAP already have a base in the Kota Melaka area, Ayer Keroh and the relevant state constituencies.
"God willing, we can reclaim our traditional seats. PKR has its own traditional seats that we have won before. The same goes for Amanah. So, we come to Melaka not just offering unrealistic ideas. We have experience," he said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka election with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
The 2021 Melaka election saw Barisan Nasional win 21 of the 28 seats contested to form the state government, while PH won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.

Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is developing a Food Safety Index to measure the effectiveness of food safety controls across the country's food supply chain.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the index would assess the overall effectiveness of the national food safety control system across three domains, government, industry and consumers.
